hypothesis: Positioning BlurPool anti-aliasing filtering immediately after ReLU non-linearities suppresses high-frequency non-linear aliasing harmonics, while integrating non-reduction Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) and enforcing a semantic minimum crop scale of 0.15 will enhance feature representation quality under Decoupled Contrastive Learning (DCL).
rationale: In iter 12, BlurPool anti-aliased downsampling on ResNet-26 achieved the current best accuracy (0.6144). However, in iter 12 BlurPool was placed before ReLU, allowing non-linear activations to re-introduce high-frequency aliasing prior to downsampling. Applying anti-aliased filtering right after ReLU filters out these non-linear spatial harmonics before spatial subsampling (Zhang 2019). Furthermore, full Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) failed in iter 4 due to severe channel compression (16x bottleneck), whereas Efficient Channel Attention (ECA, Wang et al. 2020) uses a 1D convolution over channel descriptors without channel reduction, preserving cross-channel signals at zero parameter cost. Lastly, minimum crop scales of 0.08 on 32x32 images create sub-9x9 pixel crops that destroy visual semantics; raising scale to (0.15, 1.0) guarantees that crop pairs maintain object-level semantic context.
expected_effect: Improvement in representation discriminability and positive-pair alignment, leading to higher top-1 linear evaluation accuracy on CIFAR-100.
change_summary:
1. Upgraded AntiAliasedBasicBlock to perform BlurPool anti-aliased filtering post-ReLU (after non-linear activation) and integrated an ECALayer (Efficient Channel Attention) into every block.
2. Refined get_augmentation() to use scale=(0.15, 1.0) for RandomResizedCrop and removed Gaussian blur to prevent semantic degradation on low-resolution 32x32 images.
3. Retained Decoupled Contrastive Loss (DCL, tau=0.10), 1.5x wider ResNet-26 backbone (768-dim features), 4096-wide projection head, and standard pretraining schedule.
